items.author: CoinGiggleMoe
items.context: MoeTrading (@CoinGiggleMoe, 3.104 seguidores, en inglés) pregunta abiertamente si de verdad se puede confiar en la media de 200 o 300 semanas como soporte de $BTC con solo ~850 semanas de historia, comparando con QQQ, SPX y NQ que rompieron sus medias largas con caídas de 30-40%. Pregunta abierta sobre la media de 200 semanas, ~25 min de antigüedad, 248 vistas, 5 likes y 1 sola respuesta: se responde con los datos del índice Market Temperature.
items.suggested_text:
Fair question, and sample size is the real issue. 850 weeks of history means the 200-week average has only been tested in a handful of bear markets, so each touch is closer to an anecdote than a statistic. Any single line drawn on that little data will eventually break.

That's why it works better as one input than as a floor. Price vs. the 200-week average tells you how stretched the market is, but it reads very differently when MVRV, the drawdown from the high and volatility-adjusted momentum point the same way. Our Market Temperature index weights those four at 25% each, and it went from 99.29 to 0.67 in 364 days.

The QQQ/SPX comparison is the interesting part: decades of data, and those averages still gave way. Maybe the question was never whether a level holds, but how long price can live below it.
